graph.summary: Hydroxychloroquine → Toll-like receptor 9 → type I interferon production → Systemic Lupus Erythematosus

evidence.snippet: Our data also confirm an earlier report that this same mechanism may explain inhibition of TLR7 and 9 signaling by hydroxychloroquine
evidence.explanation: Lamphier et al. confirm that hydroxychloroquine inhibits TLR7 and TLR9 signaling via accumulation in intracellular acidic compartments, the same mechanism as the novel small-molecule inhibitors studied.

paper.title: Novel small molecule inhibitors of TLR7 and TLR9: mechanism of action and efficacy in vivo.

evidence.snippet: clinically-relevant HCQ concentrations partially inhibit the pDC response to TLR9
evidence.explanation: Gardet et al. show that blood HCQ levels in CLE patients correlate with reduced ex vivo pDC response to the TLR9 agonist CpG-A, confirming HCQ decreases TLR9 signaling activity in human clinical samples.

paper.title: Effect of in vivo Hydroxychloroquine and ex vivo Anti-BDCA2 mAb Treatment on pDC IFNα Production From Patients Affected With Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus.

evidence.snippet: antimalarials also appear to have an impact through inhibition of intracellular toll-like receptors (TLRs), particularly TLR9
evidence.explanation: Katz and Russell review confirm that antimalarials including hydroxychloroquine act by inhibiting endosomal/intracellular TLRs, particularly TLR9.

paper.title: Re-evaluation of antimalarials in treating rheumatic diseases: re-appreciation and insights into new mechanisms of action.

evidence.snippet: PDCs were the only producers of IFNα in response to CpG-A, R848, and ssRNA stimulation in PBMC cultures.
evidence.explanation: CpG-A is a TLR9 agonist; that pDCs are the sole IFNα producers in response to CpG-A demonstrates that TLR9 signaling drives type I interferon (IFNα) production.

paper.title: Effect of in vivo Hydroxychloroquine and ex vivo Anti-BDCA2 mAb Treatment on pDC IFNα Production From Patients Affected With Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus.

evidence.snippet: IFN-I signaling is increased in pediatric SLE, largely due to the presence of plasmacytoid dendritic cells and pathways such as cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes-TANK-binding kinase 1 and Toll-like receptor (TLR)4/TLR9.
evidence.explanation: Zhou and Song's review identifies TLR9 as one of the primary pathways driving increased type I interferon signaling/production in SLE patients.

paper.title: Type I interferon pathway in pediatric systemic lupus erythematosus.

evidence.snippet: Aberrant and persistent production of interferon-α (IFN-α) by plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) is known to play a key role in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
evidence.explanation: Sakata et al. establish that aberrant type I interferon (IFNα) production is a key driver of SLE pathogenesis, confirming that the type I interferon production process contributes to SLE.

paper.title: Up-Regulation of TLR7-Mediated IFN-α Production by Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cells in Patients With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

evidence.snippet: nucleic acid-sensing Toll-like receptors (TLRs), and type I interferon can affect B-cell survival and decrease their threshold for activation
evidence.explanation: Singh et al. confirm that type I interferon, produced downstream of nucleic-acid-sensing TLRs, contributes to aberrant B-cell activation that underlies SLE pathogenesis.

paper.title: Interfering with baffled B cells at the lupus tollway: Promises, successes, and failed expectations.
paper.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
